findings.title: Idempotency claim result is discarded — the claim gates nothing (dead defense-in-depth layer); misleading 'Stand down' / 'never double-applies' comments
findings.evidence: case sql.claim_webhook_event(db, event_id, source) { Ok(pog.Returned(_, [_, ..])) -> Nil  Ok(_) -> { wisp.log_info("...duplicate event ignored..."); Nil }  Error(err) -> { capture(sentry, ...); Nil } }  // then unconditionally: case sql.find_reference_call_by_send_ref(...)
findings.detail: DEMOTEb from blocker. The case is a discarded expression (Gleam has no early return); every branch yields Nil and step 2 (find+mark) runs unconditionally. The 'Stand down' / 'never double-applies' comments overstate it. HOWEVER no double-apply occurs: find_reference_call_by_send_ref + mark_awaiting_correction are both scoped WHERE status IN ('queued','contact_initiated'), so a re-delivered event finds 0 rows (row is now awaiting_correction) and no-ops. resend_redelivery_is_idempotent_test asserts audit_count==1 + notification_count==1 (passes; CI green). The claim is a redundant/dead layer, not a live dedup gate.
findings.recommended_fix: Either remove the dead claim + correct the comments to describe the actual idempotency mechanism (find/mark live-status scoping), or keep it as an observability hook but document it does NOT gate. Do NOT make it early-return on 0 rows — that would turn a crash-after-claim-before-mark into a lost transition (at-most-once); the current fall-through gives better completion semantics via find/mark.

findings.title: AC8 says entity_id = vacancy, but the notification is created on the reference_call entity (mirrors the existing reference notifications)
findings.evidence: dispatch(db, landlord_id, sql.ReferenceAwaitingCorrection, title, body, "reference_call", reference_call_id,)  // sibling dispatch_reference_notification (notify_reference_unreachable etc.) ALSO uses "reference_call"/reference_call_id
findings.detail: Spec AC8 + Dev Note 3 say 'entity_id = vacancy (mirror notify_reference_unreachable)' — but notify_reference_unreachable itself uses reference_call (via dispatch_reference_notification). Spec self-contradicts; the minion mirrored the existing consistent pattern (all reference notifications use the reference_call entity). No live breakage; confirm which entity the dashboard/vacancy-panel groups on for RC4.3.
findings.recommended_fix: Clarify the spec contradiction. If the vacancy-panel badge needs vacancy scoping, switch to vacancy_id; otherwise update AC8/Dev Note 3 to say reference_call (matching the mirror).

findings.title: Missing-signature (missing-header) rejections log but don't capture to Sentry — AC3 says capture
findings.evidence: Error(reason) -> { wisp.log_warning("resend-events webhook missing svix headers: " <> reason); reject_unauthorized() }  // no sentry_client.capture — unlike the bad-signature branch which DOES capture (ResendWebhookSignatureFailed / TwilioWebhookSignatureFailed)
findings.detail: AC3 requires 'the verification failure is captured to Sentry' for 'invalid, malformed, or missing signature'. The bad-signature path IS captured; the missing-HEADER path (extract_headers Error / no X-Twilio-Signature) only log_warning. Minor observability gap on a less-suspicious code path.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a sentry_client.capture to the missing-header branches (mirror the bad-signature captures) for AC3 completeness, or amend AC3 to scope Sentry to the bad-signature path only.

findings.title: AC3's Twilio replay-window/timestamp clause is unaddressed (verifier takes no timestamp)
findings.evidence: pub fn verify_signature(auth_token, url, params, provided_signature) -> Result(Nil, Nil) { ... crypto.secure_compare(...) }  // no timestamp parameter; handler parses none
findings.detail: AC3 says reject 'for Twilio, a stale/future-tolerant timestamp outside the replay window'. Twilio's signing model has NO signed timestamp (HMAC over url+sorted params only), so this is not implementable via the signature; replay is functionally mitigated by the idempotency layer (claim_webhook_event) instead. The Resend/svix path DOES have a 5-min replay window (reused from inbound_email/svix.gleam). Literal AC text for Twilio is unmet.
findings.recommended_fix: Amend AC3 to reflect that Twilio replay protection is via idempotency (not a signed timestamp), or add an explicit Twilio timestamp-window check if a timestamp param is available in the callback.

findings.evidence: webhooks.gleam: "email.failed" -> "email_failed"   // mark_awaiting_correction.sql docstring: '-- ... email_complaint, delivery_failed, sms_failed, sms_undelivered)'   // spec AC1: 'terminal_reason is stamped (e.g. email_bounced/email_complaint/delivery_failed)'

No live consumer (rc3-7's referee_contact_invalid fraud signal isn't built yet), but the inconsistency could bite rc3-7 if it matches on the docstring/spec slug.

findings.title: notify_reference_awaiting_correction Result discarded via ignore_result — failure is logged (not Sentry'd); adjacent comment claims 'captured'
findings.evidence: notification_dispatch.notify_reference_awaiting_correction(...) |> ignore_result   // comment: 'Both are best-effort (a failure here is captured but does not roll back the transition).'   // dispatch() on Error only does wisp.log_warning, no sentry capture
findings.detail: ignore_result returns Nil for Ok and Error, so a notification insert failure is swallowed by the handler. dispatch() does log_warning internally (so it's not fully silent), but it is NOT Sentry-captured, and the 'captured' comment overstates it. Best-effort is intended (AC8), so functionally fine.
findings.recommended_fix: Soften the comment to 'logged, not Sentry-captured' for accuracy, or add a capture in the handler's Error branch if notification failures should be observable.
